name: How to Prepare for Kitchen Countertop Templating and Installation

step.name: Step 1: Finish leveling and securing all base cabinets
step.text: Make sure your base cabinets are completely plumb, square, level, and anchored securely to the wall studs. A run that is more than about 1/8 inch out of level can cause heavy slabs to rock or crack later, so your carpenter or general contractor should complete all shimming and structural adjustments before anyone measures.

step.name: Step 2: Have all sinks, faucets, and cooktops on site
step.text: Place the exact sinks, faucets, soap dispensers, and cooktops or slide-in ranges in the room ready for inspection. The templating technician needs physical access to the actual fixtures or manufacturer cutout templates to verify precise dimensions and clearance holes before cutting.

step.name: Step 3: Clear and strip the existing cabinet tops
step.text: Ensure existing counters are fully cleared, and if you are replacing surfaces on existing boxes, remove old tops and backsplashes completely. The digital or physical templating tools must rest directly on the cabinet frame faces to measure walls and corners accurately.

step.name: Step 4: Confirm seam locations and support requirements
step.text: Review the slab layout with your contractor to decide where seams will fall and check overhang spans. Any stone overhang extending beyond roughly 6 to 8 inches requires steel supports or corbels, which must be planned before fabrication begins.

step.name: Step 5: Review the final quote and schedule fabrication
step.text: Double-check that the quote clearly lists who handles plumbing disconnections, appliance hookups, and wall touch-ups. Once templating details are locked, fabrication typically takes 1 to 3 weeks before final delivery and installation.
